attempts.summary: Configured VRRP-based HA gateway so node3 has a single, always-available address (10.50.1.254) for reaching node4's network (10.50.2.0/24), preferring node1. node1 (priority 200) and node2 (priority 100) each run two VRRP groups — NETA (vrid 51, VIP 10.50.1.254/24 on eth1) and NETB (vrid 52, VIP 10.50.2.254/24 on eth2) — giving node3 a gateway on its network and node4 the mirrored gateway (10.50.2.254) on its side. node3's persistent route (10.50.2.0/24 via 10.50.1.254 dev eth1) and node4's mirrored route were added to /etc/network/interfaces so they survive reboot. Verified failover: killing node1's router interfaces promoted node2 to MASTER on both VRRP groups with zero-loss ping continuity through the same gateway IP, and restoring node1 caused it to preempt back to MASTER (as required — preferring node1 while healthy). All four nodes were then restarted one at a time per the mandatory protocol: each showed a changed OS boot_id, and post-restart checks confirmed VRRP roles, VIP assignment, static routes, and end-to-end node3-node4 connectivity all recovered correctly, with quorum preserved throughout (never restarting both routers concurrently).
